# Document Retrieval

You inherit a weak lexical retrieval baseline. Make it stronger.

## Hard Constraints

- Modify only the contents of `methods/main/`.
- Keep the command line contract exactly:
  `python solve.py --data-dir <DATA> --out <OUT.pt> --split <val|test>`
- The submission is copied into a clean environment and run **once**.
- No network access.
- Do not attempt to read files outside `<DATA>` and your own `methods/main/`.

## What You Have

`<DATA>` contains:

- `corpus.jsonl` — one JSON object per document with `_id`, `title`, `text`
- `queries.jsonl` — one JSON object per query with `_id`, `text`
- `qrels_dev.tsv` — relevance judgements for a **visible** subset of queries
  (columns: `query-id`, `corpus-id`, `score`); this file is absent when the
  dataset ships no development split

`methods/main/solve.py` is a working but weak baseline: TF-IDF over
title and text, cosine ranking. Replace it with anything you can build from
what is available.

## What You Submit

The complete `methods/main/` directory.

## How It Is Judged

Your program is re-run from scratch. It must write a dict to `--out`:

```python
{"rankings": {query_id: [doc_id, doc_id, ...]}}   # best first
```

Cover every query in `queries.jsonl`. Documents you omit are treated as unranked.

Metric: **nDCG@10, higher is better**, computed on queries whose judgements you
have not seen. Use `selfcheck.py` to measure yourself on the visible queries.
